title: Audit ingest migration: staged backfill, TTL heuristics & cost-safety gating
creator: Maya Chen
description: Migrate the audit ingest pipeline from the legacy monolith to the new tiered ingestion system with a staged backfill process. Implement tenant-aware TTL heuristics and cost-safety gating to ensure historical backfills do not violate quotas or cause downstream hot shards. Denormalize RBAC v2 change events for faster audit queries and ensure SSO/SAML admin events are preserved intact during compaction. The work includes a staging backfill runner, quota-aware rate limiter, compaction rules for the compact index, and dashboards to detect backfill-induced QoS regressions.
acceptance_criteria: Staging backfill runner can replay 30 days of audit events for a single org without exceeding configured tenant backfill bandwidth
Backfill job respects tenant quotas and global cost-safety window; backfill throttles when cost budget > 90%
Compaction policy reduces index size by at least 35% on backfilled segments while preserving required RBAC/SAML fields for compliance
End-to-end integration tests for denormalized RBAC v2 events ensure query parity with legacy store for 95% of common audit queries
Monitoring dashboard shows no increase in producer error rate or 99p tail latency on ingestion during staged backfill runs
implementation_notes: Add a staging backfill orchestrator component that can run per-tenant backfills with configurable concurrency and rate limits
Implement tenant-aware leaky-bucket rate limiter tied to billing/commit usage; surface throttling events to chargeback dashboard
Introduce TTL heuristic: default 90d, extra retention for privileged RBAC changes and SSO admin events with tag-based override
Compact index strategy: time-first partitioning with sub-partitioning by tenant hash to limit hot-shard amplification
Denormalize RBAC v2 events during ingest: expand role bindings and user metadata into event envelopes to avoid heavy join paths on read
Ensure backfill can be surgical: support include/exclude filters by event_type (e.g., SAML_ASSERTION, RBAC_CHANGE, SESSION_ADMIN) to reduce cost
rollout_steps: 1) Deploy backfill runner to staging with feature flag and run 7-day backfill for internal orgs
2) Validate compact index reduction and query parity against baseline; collect metrics for cost and latency
3) Enable tenant-aware throttling in staging; simulate heavy concurrent backfills to tune leaky-bucket params
4) Soft-launch for a single pilot customer org with explicit opt-in and monitoring
5) Gradually increase pilot scope after 72h stability window and SLA checks
6) GA: remove feature flag and document retention overrides and admin controls in Console
testing_notes: Create synthetic workload generator that replays production audit streams with preserved timestamp distribution
Fuzz-tests compaction to ensure no RBAC v2 or SAML fields are lost after compaction/denormalization
Add end-to-end smoke tests: ingest -> backfill -> compact -> query returns same event counts for key queries
Introduce chaos test to kill backfill workers mid-run and assert safe resume semantics and idempotency
Load-test leaky-bucket under heavy tenant concurrency to surface fairness and starvation edge cases
